check: whether any test method contains no assertion, re-run because the suite grew by 76 tests since the last check
why: An assertion-free test is counted as coverage while checking nothing - the same shape as the filtered-stream assertions fixed last round. The suite gained 76 tests this session, so the earlier clean result needed re-running rather than re-citing.
method: Walked every @Test and @GameTest method body by brace depth and flagged those containing no assert, require, fail, rejects or assertThrows call.

andAllTwentyFiveAreDelegationsRatherThan.checked: Each flagged body's called methods were extracted, and the callee inspected for assertions in its own file
examples: MulDivFastPathTest.integerFastPathAndWideFallbackMatchIndependentFloorDivision loops over edge values and random inputs calling a private verify(a,b,d) that asserts
LootResourceTest's four flagged methods each call a private chest(name, min, max, items) helper that asserts weights and counts
CurvedGateRegressionTests and CurvedSiteMatrixTests are one-line wrappers delegating to AdjacentComponentMatrixTests.curvedGateRegression and curvedHeightSitePairs
FringeOwnerCoverageTests delegates to a ProductionPipeline path, HydroBoundaryRegressionTests to touchingNarrowWaterRegression
WallArchPreparationGameTests delegates through its fixture builder, which is the same class whose other cases assert directly
andAllTwentyFiveAreDelegationsRatherThan.theHeaviestCallee: AdjacentComponentMatrixTests holds 158 assertion statements and is the target of several of these wrappers, which is why its wrappers look bare

conclusion: No test in the suite is assertion-free. The flagged set is a delegation pattern: thin named cases that exist so each matrix or helper appears as a discrete, individually reported test.
whyThePatternIsReasonable: It gives the failure output a meaningful test name rather than one matrix case reporting under a generic method, at the cost that reading a single file no longer shows what is checked.
whatThisRoundsOut: Together with the trivially-true assertion search, which found nothing, and the filtered-stream fix, the suite now has no known way for a test to be counted while checking nothing.
